**BNP Paribas and HSBC complete first corporate payment on Swift's shared ledger**

*The shift from pilot to production use of Swift's distributed ledger – marked by a Siemens treasury transaction – is a milestone for banks exploring tokenised settlement infrastructure.*

BNP Paribas and HSBC have executed the first corporate treasury payment on Swift's blockchain-based shared ledger, processing a transaction for Siemens. The move takes the ledger – first announced in September 2025 and opened to live bank pilots in July – from controlled testing into live corporate use.

Swift had previously confirmed that banks would begin piloting live transactions on the platform, but the involvement of a major corporate treasury operation gives the initiative a practical reference point. Siemens treasury chief Joerg Bermuller has been among the most vocal corporate advocates for open banking standards in payments infrastructure, and the company's participation signals genuine demand from the buy side.

The transaction demonstrates that Swift's approach – layering distributed ledger technology onto existing correspondent banking relationships – can handle real corporate flows. The gap between prototype and production has narrowed, though whether this model scales to high-volume treasury operations remains an open question.

*Sources: [BNP Paribas and HSBC complete first corporate treasury transaction on Swift's blockchain ledger](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48347/bnp-paribas-and-hsbc-complete-first-corporate-treasury-transaction-on-swifts-blockchain-ledger?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Pay.UK warns AI-driven fraud is the fastest-moving threat to UK payments**

*David Crawford, Pay.UK's chief strategy and transformation officer, frames AI-generated fraud as outpacing current defences and links it to the proposed merger of the PSR into the FCA.*

David Crawford, Pay.UK's chief strategy and transformation officer, has identified AI-driven fraud as the most rapidly evolving risk facing the UK payments system. Crawford said the speed and sophistication of AI-generated scams are advancing faster than the industry's capacity to detect them, creating a widening gap between attackers and defenders.

Crawford placed the fraud challenge alongside broader structural shifts, including the proposed merger of the Payment Systems Regulator into the Financial Conduct Authority under the Financial Services and Markets Bill. That consolidation – still subject to parliamentary scrutiny – would reshape how fraud policy and payments oversight interact in the UK.

The warning reinforces a pattern visible across European payments: as instant payment volumes grow and new rails such as open banking expand the attack surface, the fraud tooling question becomes increasingly urgent. UK fraud losses rose to £1.3 billion in the most recent reporting period, with authorised push payment scams rebounding sharply after mandatory reimbursement rules took effect.

*Sources: [Pay.UK's David Crawford: AI fraud Is The Fastest-Moving Shift](https://thefintechtimes.com/pay-uks-david-crawford-ai-fraud-is-the-fastest-moving-shift/) — The Fintech Times*

**Wero goes live in Luxembourg with first in-store payments capability**

*The launch makes Luxembourg EPI's fifth market and – through the Payconiq migration – the first where Wero supports point-of-sale acceptance, a milestone in the scheme's progression beyond peer-to-peer and e-commerce.*

The European Payments Initiative (EPI) held a press conference in Luxembourg on September 2 to mark the start of the Payconiq-to-Wero migration. Throughout September, Wero is becoming progressively available to Luxembourg consumers and merchants as the country's five participating banks – BGL BNP Paribas, Banque Internationale a Luxembourg, Raiffeisen, Spuerkeess and Post Luxembourg – move through the different phases of the transition. Payconiq's platform will shut permanently on September 30, giving users and merchants a single month to switch.

The migration matters beyond Luxembourg's 300,000 Payconiq users because it introduces a capability Wero has lacked elsewhere: in-store payments. In Germany, France and Belgium, Wero has operated as a peer-to-peer and e-commerce tool. By absorbing Payconiq's established QR-code merchant network, Luxembourg becomes the first market where Wero functions at the physical point of sale. Existing Payconiq QR codes on invoices and in shops will remain scannable via the Wero app until the end of 2026, with merchants required to replace them with Wero-branded codes by the end of September.

Hakan Sekulu, chief executive of Worldline in Luxembourg, said success depends on strong customer adoption, easy integration and frictionless checkout. The compressed timetable – one month of parallel running before Payconiq closes – will test whether EPI's approach of coordinated, market-wide switchovers can deliver a smoother transition than the gradual rollouts seen in its other markets.

*Sources: [Payconiq Payment System Officially Transitions to Wero Platform in Luxembourg](https://www.chronicle.lu/category/banking/63148-payconiq-payment-system-officially-transitions-to-wero-platform-in-luxembourg) — Chronicle.lu*
